evidence.B1: src/webhook_receiver/signature.py:75 `return hmac.compare_digest(received, expected.digest())`. No `==` comparison of digests anywhere; the raw-hex is decoded to bytes first (signature.py:70) so the compare is over fixed-length bytes.
evidence.B2: src/webhook_receiver/signature.py:78-99 `check_timestamp` parses the header and returns STALE/FUTURE outside `tolerance` (default 300 s, signature.py:20); src/webhook_receiver/service.py:104-106 calls it and returns 400 before any HMAC work. Live: a timestamp 4000 s in the past with an otherwise valid signature returned `(400, '{"error":"stale_timestamp",...}')`. Boundary behaviour asserted in tests/unit/test_signature.py:104-116 (±299/±300 accepted, ±301 rejected).
evidence.B3: src/webhook_receiver/store.py:43 `UNIQUE (sender_id, delivery_id)` plus store.py:171 `ON CONFLICT (sender_id, delivery_id) DO NOTHING ... RETURNING` — the insert itself decides, so there is no check-then-write window. Identity comes from the `X-Webhook-Delivery` header (service.py:114-119). tests/unit/test_store.py:43-51 asserts that identical payloads with different delivery ids are distinct and that the same id from different senders is distinct; tests/integration/test_service.py:167-181 fires 8 concurrent coroutines on the same key and asserts exactly one 202, seven 200s, one handler call. Live: second POST of `d1` -> `200 duplicate`.
evidence.B4: src/webhook_receiver/app.py:60-73 `_read_limited` accumulates raw `bytes` off `request.stream()`; those bytes go straight to `service.receive(body=corpo)` (app.py:128) and into `canonical_message` (signature.py:32-45), which takes `bytes` only — the module docstring at signature.py:5-6 states nothing accepts `str` for exactly this reason. The body is never json-parsed at the HTTP layer. tests/unit/test_signature.py:68-77 signs `{"cliente":"Ação Ltda","valor":10,"nota":"café"}` and asserts a re-serialised equivalent object fails verification. Live confirmation: a non-JSON body (`nao e json <<>>`) with a valid signature was accepted 202.
evidence.B5: src/webhook_receiver/app.py:141-147 attaches `BackgroundTask(service.dispatch, resultado.delivery)` to the response; `service.receive` explicitly does not run the handler (service.py:100-103). tests/e2e/test_resposta_rapida.py:74-96 uses a real uvicorn server (not ASGITransport, which would mask this) with a 2 s handler and asserts response < 0.2 s and `handler.concluidos == 0`. I reproduced it independently against a real uvicorn with a 2 s handler, including over a reused keep-alive connection: `keepalive req0 202 0.008s / req1 202 0.001s / req2 202 0.001s`, so there is no head-of-line blocking either.
evidence.C1: src/webhook_receiver/service.py:110 returns `Outcome(401, Reason.UNAUTHORIZED, log_reason="bad_signature")` — the reason goes to the log only (app.py:135-139), never the body. src/webhook_receiver/signature.py:54-61 returns a bare bool so missing/malformed/wrong cannot be distinguished by the caller. tests/e2e/test_http.py:70-88 posts five different failure variants (zeroed hex, no prefix, non-hex, wrong secret, header absent) and asserts the response bodies and even their byte lengths are identical after stripping the trace. Live: `(401, '{"error":"unauthorized","trace":...}')` for both a bad signature and a cross-sender signature.
evidence.C2: The body is never parsed at the HTTP layer, so a malformed body cannot raise there. Live: POST of `nao e json <<>>` with a valid signature -> 202, and the server log line was `failed sender=acme delivery=d5 attempt=1 reason=JSONDecodeError` — no 500, no traceback, no leak. Empty body -> 202 likewise. This is a deliberate choice documented at src/webhook_receiver/handlers.py:61-68 (a 400 would make an authentic sender retry forever) and asserted in tests/e2e/test_http.py:213-223. Only the exception *type* is recorded, never the message (service.py:150-152).
evidence.C3: Missing timestamp -> `TimestampProblem.MISSING` (signature.py:89-90) -> 400 `missing_timestamp`, asserted tests/e2e/test_http.py:107-111. Unparseable timestamp -> signature.py:91-92 `raw.isascii() and raw.isdigit()` -> 400 `malformed_timestamp`; live: `X-Webhook-Timestamp: zzz` -> `(400, '{"error":"malformed_timestamp",...}')`. Missing signature -> 401 (signature.py:62). Repeated security headers -> app.py:112-115 rejects with 400 `duplicate_header` rather than picking one arbitrarily (tests/e2e/test_http.py:182-189). Over-long/non-printable delivery id -> 400 `invalid_delivery_id` (service.py:65-68, 119).
evidence.C4: src/webhook_receiver/service.py:147-167 wraps the handler call; on exception it calls `store.mark_failed` (store.py:240-274), which increments attempts, sets exponential backoff and releases the lease, so the row and its payload survive. src/webhook_receiver/recovery.py:38-48 re-claims it. Live: two deliveries whose handler raised were logged `failed ... reason=JSONDecodeError` and /health then reported `pending: 2` — the deliveries were retained, not lost, and the process kept serving. tests/integration/test_service.py:198-208 asserts status PENDING / attempts 1 / last_error, :210-218 asserts a failing delivery does not affect the next one, :264-283 asserts the payload is still intact after reaching dead-letter.
evidence.D1: `/tmp/venvD/bin/python -m pytest -q` on a fresh venv built from the checkout: `153 passed in 5.85s`. No skips, no warnings (pyproject.toml:33 sets `filterwarnings = ["error"]`).
evidence.D2: tests/e2e/test_http.py:36-41 posts a signed body through the real ASGI app and asserts 202 + envelope + content-type; tests/e2e/test_http.py:232-237 asserts the handler actually received it with the right delivery id; tests/e2e/test_resposta_rapida.py:74-96 does the same against a real uvicorn server and asserts the row reaches `Status.HANDLED`.
evidence.D3: Signature rejection: tests/e2e/test_http.py:62-67 and :70-88. Replay/staleness: tests/e2e/test_http.py:91-104 parametrised over stale/future/malformed/empty, tests/unit/test_signature.py:104-127, tests/integration/test_service.py:107-118. Duplicate delivery: tests/e2e/test_http.py:55-59, tests/integration/test_service.py:82-91, and the concurrent 8-way race at tests/integration/test_service.py:167-181.
evidence.D4: Tests assert observable outcomes — status codes, envelope slugs, `Allow` headers, handler invocation counts, persisted row status/attempts. Several assert properties the implementation could not fake: tests/e2e/test_http.py:70-88 asserts equal *byte lengths* of all 401 bodies; :318-333 asserts a card number, CVV, signature and secret never appear in any log line; :260-265 asserts /health leaks no sender or payload; tests/unit/test_store.py:65 and :201 use real multi-thread contention rather than mocks. Only one test reaches into internals in a way that restates implementation (tests/unit/test_store.py:59-62 asserting the pragma values), and that is checking a durability guarantee, not a shape.
evidence.E1: The decision is structural, not commented-in. `service.receive` returns an `Outcome` and deliberately does not call the handler (src/webhook_receiver/service.py:100-103); the edge attaches dispatch as a `BackgroundTask` after building the response (app.py:141-147); the consequence of that choice — a delivery that is recorded but never dispatched if the process dies — is paid for by a lease column (store.py:41-42) and a recovery loop wired into the app lifespan (app.py:206-222, recovery.py:25-64). The at-least-once contract this creates is stated in the handler Protocol docstring (handlers.py:39-56) and in the README (lines 70-74). The layer split is enforced by the test structure: tests/integration/ exercises the core with no HTTP at all.
evidence.E2: src/webhook_receiver/config.py declares only the *name* of the env var in TOML (`secret_env`, config.py:19) and reads the value from the passed-in environment (config.py:131-146); nothing is defaulted or inlined. `Sender.secret` is `field(repr=False)` (config.py:43) so it cannot leak via a repr. Test secrets live only in test fixtures. tests/e2e/test_cli.py:60-67 asserts `check` never prints a secret value; I confirmed live — `webhook-receiver check` printed `segredo de WEBHOOK_SECRET_ACME`, the variable name, not the value. tests/e2e/test_http.py:318-333 asserts the secret never reaches the log.
evidence.E3: Partially met. I ran the project start to finish using only the README: venv + `pip install -e ".[dev]"` (README:88-92), the `webhook-receiver.toml` from README:98-108, the `export WEBHOOK_SECRET_*` lines from README:112-115, `webhook-receiver check` (README:122) -> `configuração ok — 2 emissores`, `webhook-receiver serve` (README:130) -> server up, `/health` returning the documented shape. That part works. What the documentation does not give: the README's own curl example (README:144-150) leaves `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<hmac-sha256-hex>` undefined — the canonical signed message (`timestamp + "." + body`, src/webhook_receiver/signature.py:45) and the `v1=` prefix convention appear nowhere in the README, so a reader cannot construct a valid delivery or implement a sender without reading the source. The README is also visibly truncated in three places (line 7-8 "e a suíte\nsegundos.", line 183 "…o texto exato das mensagens, está" ending mid-reference at a document that does not exist in the repo, line 253 "Mudanças que alterem verificação de assinatura, deduplicação ou o contrato do").

unanticipated_findings: README.md is truncated in three places, and one truncation drops a cross-reference to a document that does not exist in the repo. Line 7-8 reads "...e a suíte\nsegundos." with the verb and number missing. Line 183 reads "A superfície completa, com todos os estados e o texto exato das mensagens, está" and then simply stops — the reader is pointed at a spec that was never written and is not in the tree (there is no docs/ directory; `find` over the repo returns only src/, tests/, .github/, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, LICENSE, pyproject.toml, .gitignore). Line 253 reads "Mudanças que alterem verificação de assinatura, deduplicação ou o contrato do" and stops. The same defect appears in source: src/webhook_receiver/cli.py:4 begins mid-sentence with "governam tudo aqui:" — the subject of the sentence is gone. Reproduce: `sed -n '4,9p;182,185p;252,255p' README.md` and `sed -n '1,7p' src/webhook_receiver/cli.py`.

The signing contract is undocumented outside the source. The README shows `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<hmac-sha256-hex>` (README:148) but never states what bytes are HMAC'd. The actual canonical message is `timestamp.encode('ascii') + b'.' + body` (src/webhook_receiver/signature.py:45) with a mandatory `v1=` prefix and a strict 64-hex-char length check (signature.py:62-67). A sender team handed this README cannot implement signing; every one of their deliveries would return an opaque 401 that, by design (service.py:110), tells them nothing. This is the one place where the deliberate no-oracle 401 policy and the documentation gap compound into a real integration hazard.

`webhook-receiver check` creates the database file as a side effect, contradicting its own documented contract. README:117-119 describes check as validating and exiting "sem iniciar nada" (starting nothing), and cli.py:53 advertises it as "valida a configuração e sai, sem subir nada". But comando_check calls `_abrir_banco(args.db)` (cli.py:117), which runs `store.initialize()` (cli.py:64-66) and executes the CREATE TABLE script. Reproduce: `mkdir /tmp/x && cd /tmp/x && cp <config> . && webhook-receiver check` — `ls` afterwards shows `deliveries.db` (plus `-wal` and `-shm` after any subsequent serve) in a directory that had none. I observed exactly this in /tmp/rundD. It is arguably intentional (it is how writability is proven) but it is not what the docs promise, and it means running the deploy-time preflight check against a production path silently creates a file.

Two pieces of dead code that a reader will trip over. (a) `TimestampProblem` is imported at src/webhook_receiver/service.py:23 and never referenced — service.py:106 converts via `Reason(problema.value)` instead. Verified: `grep -n "TimestampProblem" src/webhook_receiver/service.py` returns only line 23. (b) `DeliveryStore.mark_handled(self, row_id: int, now: float)` (src/webhook_receiver/store.py:229) declares and requires a `now` parameter that the SQL body (store.py:230-238) never uses — the UPDATE binds only `(Status.HANDLED.value, row_id)`. Both callers (service.py:169, and the tests) pass a clock value that is discarded. Harmless today, but the signature implies a handled_at timestamp is being recorded, and it is not — there is no completion-time column in the schema at all (store.py:31-44), so a dead-letter or latency post-mortem cannot tell when a delivery was actually processed.

All SQLite work runs synchronously on the asyncio event loop thread with `synchronous = FULL` (store.py:121) — `store.record` on the accept path (service.py:122), `store.counts` on /health (app.py:153), and `mark_handled`/`mark_failed` in dispatch. Nothing is offloaded with `asyncio.to_thread` (the only such offload in the codebase is inside JsonlHandler, handlers.py:86, for the file write). Under a slow or contended fsync, the accept path blocks the whole loop and the fast-2xx property that the design is built around degrades globally. The project's own latency test (tests/e2e/test_resposta_rapida.py:99-121) measures this only sequentially on a local tmpfs-backed path, so it would not surface the failure mode; my own p99 was likewise fine locally. Recorded as an unmeasured risk, not a demonstrated failure.

`store.record` relies on `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING ... RETURNING` (store.py:165-183) and `claim_due` on `UPDATE ... RETURNING` (store.py:204-226). `RETURNING` requires SQLite 3.35+ (March 2021). Neither pyproject.toml nor the README states a minimum SQLite version, and there is no startup check — `webhook-receiver check` (cli.py:106-131) only opens the database and runs the CREATE TABLE script, which succeeds on older SQLite. On a host with an older bundled libsqlite3, the service would pass `check` cleanly and then fail at runtime on the first delivery, surfacing as a 503 storage_unavailable (app.py:130-133) rather than a startup error. Not reproducible here (my Python 3.14 links a new enough SQLite and all 153 tests pass), so this is a portability gap rather than an observed break.
